papers.title: Superconducting singlet-triplet qubits
papers.abstract: Hybrid devices integrating quantum dots with Josephson junctions are gaining interest because they combine spin-based quantum computing with circuit quantum electrodynamics (circuit QED) methods. In particular, Andreev spin qubits have shown significant experimental progress including strong two-qubit coupling, and are predicted to exhibit all-to-all connectivity. Here we propose superconducting singlet-triplet (SST) qubits that rely on parallel-aligned double quantum dots in Josephson junctions. While Andreev spin qubits require spin-orbit interaction to unlock the spin degree-of-freedom, SST qubits do not require spin-orbit interaction, making the advantages of hybrid devices available to a wider range of materials. Similar to Andreev spin qubits, the qubit states couple to the superconducting phase across the junction, which allows for control and readout using circuit QED, and supports all-to-all connectivity. Only $N$ flux lines are required to perform any single- and two-qubit gate among $N$ qubits, and thus the overhead of control lines is small. Finally, linear protection from charge or flux noise makes these qubits interesting candidates for a future quantum processor.

similar_to.title: Observation of high coherence in Josephson junction qubits measured in a three-dimensional circuit QED architecture

summary.summary: This work proposes superconducting singlet-triplet (SST) qubits—hybrid devices based on parallel-aligned double quantum dots in Josephson junctions—that combine spin-based quantum computing with circuit QED while avoiding the need for spin-orbit interaction. The SST qubits achieve all-to-all connectivity using only $N$ flux lines for $N$ qubits and exhibit linear protection against charge and flux noise.
summary.motivation: Andreev spin qubits have shown strong experimental progress in hybrid superconductor-semiconductor devices, but they require spin-orbit coupling to access the spin degree of freedom, limiting their material platforms. A platform that retains the advantages of Andreev qubits—long-range coupling and circuit QED compatibility—while working in materials lacking intrinsic spin-orbit coupling would enable broader implementation of hybrid superconducting spin qubits.
summary.method: Two quantum dots in parallel within a Josephson junction are coupled via crossed Andreev processes, with the interaction strength $E_\mathrm{CA} = 2\Gamma^2/|\epsilon|$ (where $\Gamma = \rho_F \pi t^2$) controlled by the superconducting phase $\phi$ across the junction. A magnetic field gradient creates a Zeeman energy difference $\delta h$ between dots. The resulting qubit Hamiltonian $H_\mathrm{DDJJ}' = \frac{E_\mathrm{CA}}{2}[1+\cos(\phi)](\tau^x-1) + \frac{\delta h}{2}\tau^z$ is derived from second-order perturbation theory in the large-$\mathcal{U}$ limit.
summary.result: Single-qubit gates are realized by setting $\phi=0$ (X set point) or $\phi=\pi$ (OFF set point) with arbitrary rotations achieved via flux pulses. Two-qubit gates with $\tau_j^x \tau_k^x$ interaction arise at $\phi_j=\phi_k=\pi/2$ (INT set point), enabling controlled-Z gates with duration $T = \pi\hbar E_J/(E_\mathrm{CA}^j E_\mathrm{CA}^k)$ when $\delta h \ll E_\mathrm{CA}^j E_\mathrm{CA}^k/E_J$. The idle OFF state is protected to linear order against flux noise ($\cos(\phi)$ expansion suppresses first-order fluctuations) and charge noise variations affecting tunnel couplings (quadratic protection from $\delta\Gamma$ corrections).
